_readme: KNOWN CLOSINGS WE CAME ACROSS BY HAND, BEFORE A DAILY CENSUS COULD WATCH THEM.
A census detects a closing by absence: a store drops off its own locator and, after N
collected days, is dated closed (see events.py). That only works for chains with a live
locator, and only from the day we started reading it. Everything here predates that, or
belongs to a chain we track by hand — closings found in field notes, press and the chains'
own 'first_outlet (now closed)' admissions in companies.json, assembled so the project's
point — that chains open AND quietly close — is backed by data, not only prose.
These NEVER enter stores, observations or events, and are NOT drawn on the map: a closed
store is, by definition, no longer a place that exists, and the map shows only what does.
They are a dated historical record, not a live signal.
HONESTY OVER PRECISION. We record only closings with a concrete identity. `address` is the
street when we have it and null when we only know the city; `closed_on` is an ISO date only
when it is actually known, otherwise null with the evidence in `closed_note`. `confidence`
is 'confirmed' for an explicit closed admission/record and 'uncertain' for 'appears closed'.
Aggregate retreats we cannot pin to an address (Yang's broad US withdrawal; Taier's and
Meizhou Dongpo's earlier LA-area outlets) are described in companies.json, not invented here.
SCOPE. Rows are US unless a `country` field (ISO-2) says otherwise, in which case `state` holds
the province or region. Non-US rows are kept here only as an internal record behind the
international register's prose — they are out of scope for the US map and are never shown.
A closing graduates the other way from a sighting: once a chain's live locator covers the
site, the census owns its open/closed state and the hand record here can be retired.
DISCREPANCY EVIDENCE (collected chains that keep listing a closed store). When a closure cannot be
caught by absence because the brand's own locator still lists the site, the row carries structured
evidence: `known_closed_on` (first date we had a closure signal), `still_listed` / `still_listed_
through` (that the operator still showed it open, and through what date), and `observations` — each a
dated, sourced signal with a `method`. A third-party listing (e.g. a Google 'Permanently closed'
banner) is recorded ONLY from a screenshot a person captured by hand (method 'manual_screenshot'),
never an automated query or scrape, to stay within that platform's terms; the screenshot is filed to
the internal evidence store and referenced by `evidence_ref`.
Each such discrepancy is stamped into the tamper-evident ledger manual/provenance_ledger.jsonl, so we
can later prove we knew a store was closed on a date its operator still listed it open. Verify the
chain with `python -m chain_atlas provenance`. Per-location discrepancy detail built on this is
Pro-tier and is exported only to the access-controlled location, never to the public map/data.

closings.name: Glendale (Brand Blvd) — only US store
closings.closed_note: US entry-and-exit. Bobobaba is the US-customized bubble-tea line of Amanda Wang, founder of Ningji Lemon Tea (柠季, Changsha, Hunan; 3,000+ China stores; Tencent/ByteDance-backed) — China origin, in scope. This Glendale shop was her first and ONLY US outlet, opened mid-April 2026, and closed within months: Yelp lists it CLOSED (updated Sep 2026) while Google and Apple Maps show 'Temporarily closed' (observed 7 Oct 2026). With no US outlet operating, the chain is closed in the US for now — a clean enter-and-exit example. Revisit if it reopens.
closings.source: Yelp ('BOBOBABA - CLOSED', updated Sep 2026) + Google & Apple Maps ('Temporarily closed'), hand-noted from screenshots (7 Oct 2026); press — Chinese-tea-brands-in-US coverage (Ningji's Amanda Wang; first overseas outlet opened in LA as Bobobaba, mid-April 2026).

closings.name: Flushing (Roosevelt Ave) — 1st US store
closings.closed_note: The brand's first US store (per Eater), now shown Permanently Closed. First Lamb Shabu 老诚一锅 is a Beijing lamb-spine (羊蝎子) hot pot chain (chairman Yan Zhichao; ~131 Beijing + ~58 other-China stores, mostly franchised) — China origin, in scope. It opened two NYC outlets and has since exited the US (no operating US store now) — a clean enter-and-exit. Note: the name 老诚一锅 is heavily counterfeited in China (trademark disputes), but the US operation (laochengyiguo.us) was press-confirmed as the Beijing brand's own expansion. Revisit if it reopens.
closings.source: Eater NY venue page ('First Lamb Shabu 老诚一锅' — Permanently Closed, ny.eater.com/venue/52213) + eattheworldnyc review (Dec 2017); Yelp (location reported closed). Hand-noted from screenshots 14 Oct 2026.
